ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The large rectangle in the figure is divided into three horizontal regions: the upper row has 2 identical small rectangles placed horizontally, the middle row has 5 identical small rectangles placed vertically, and the lower row has 2 identical small rectangles placed horizontally, for a total of 9 identical small rectangles. Reasoning: The long side of each small rectangle is 10 cm; let the short side be x cm. Looking from the upper row, the width of the large rectangle is equal to 2 long sides, so the width is 2×10=20 cm; looking from the middle row, the same width is equal to 5 short sides, so 5x=20, giving x=4. The height of the large rectangle is equal to the sum of the short side x in the upper row, the long side 10 of the vertically placed rectangle in the middle, and the short side x in the lower row, namely 4+10+4=18 cm. Therefore, the perimeter of the large rectangle is 2×(20+18)=76 cm.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as three horizontal bands: the top band has 2 identical rectangles laid horizontally, the middle band has 5 identical rectangles stood vertically, and the bottom band has 2 identical rectangles laid horizontally. From the text, each small rectangle has long side 10 cm. Let the short side be x. The full width of the large rectangle is both 2 long sides from the top/bottom rows and 5 short sides from the middle row, so 2·10 = 5x, giving x = 4. Then the large rectangle is 20 cm wide and has height x + 10 + x = 18 cm. Perimeter = 2(20 + 18) = 76 cm.
